story.title: U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years
story.summary: The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years, as reported by international health officials. This loss is attributed to a resurgence of measles, primarily among unvaccinated populations, marking the highest transmission rates in over 30 years. The Pan American Health Organization confirmed that the U.S. and Mexico have both lost their measles-free status.

event_overview.title: About Death Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Death Outbreak
event_overview.summary: This event is the renewed U.S. measles outbreak activity that began escalating in 2025 and continued through 2026, involving multiple state and local outbreaks rather than one single, geographically bounded incident. It includes both the health effects of sustained transmission and the public-health consequences of the United States no longer meeting the standard for measles elimination.

facts.label: Timeframe and geography
facts.value: The resurgence spans the United States, with large outbreaks reported since early 2025 and continued transmission during 2026; CDC’s national surveillance aggregates reports from state, local, tribal, and territorial jurisdictions.

facts.label: What counts as an outbreak
facts.value: For its national reporting, CDC defines a measles outbreak as three or more related cases; this means the wider event consists of numerous separate outbreaks and transmission chains.

facts.label: Public-health leadership
facts.value: State and local health departments lead case and outbreak investigations. CDC receives notified cases, monitors national data, provides laboratory and technical support, and can deploy assistance at the request of jurisdictions.

facts.label: Elimination standard
facts.value: Measles elimination means no continuous endemic transmission in a defined geographic area for at least 12 months with a well-performing surveillance system; re-established endemic transmission is a continuous chain lasting at least 12 months after prior elimination.

facts.label: Status change
facts.value: The United States had been declared free of endemic measles transmission in 2000. On November 17, 2026, CDC said it was working with partners to stop outbreaks and regain elimination status.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks notable developments tied to the U.S. measles resurgence, including deaths and the elimination-status decision, rather than every case, local outbreak, exposure notice, or public-health response.

explore_lenses.label: What does losing elimination status mean?
explore_lenses.title: Sustained local spread is back
explore_lenses.summary: The designation does not mean measles was never absent or that every U.S. resident is equally exposed; it means health officials found one chain of domestic transmission had persisted long enough to meet the threshold for endemic transmission.

claims.text: PAHO’s review found that a measles transmission chain beginning January 20, 2025 had continued in the United States for more than 12 months, which it said was sufficient to classify the country as having re-established endemic measles transmission.
PAHO says elimination status is lost when endemic transmission is re-established; the United States’ rubella and congenital-rubella-syndrome elimination status remains unchanged.
CDC Director Erica Schwartz argues that the designation itself is not what protects people, and that vaccination and stopping outbreaks remain the operative public-health measures.

points: PAHO’s review found that a measles transmission chain beginning January 20, 2025 had continued in the United States for more than 12 months, which it said was sufficient to classify the country as having re-established endemic measles transmission.
PAHO says elimination status is lost when endemic transmission is re-established; the United States’ rubella and congenital-rubella-syndrome elimination status remains unchanged.
CDC Director Erica Schwartz argues that the designation itself is not what protects people, and that vaccination and stopping outbreaks remain the operative public-health measures.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The status determination establishes sustained transmission through the PAHO review period, but it does not by itself quantify a person’s current risk in a particular state or community.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: Who is most affected by renewed spread?
explore_lenses.title: Risk concentrates where protection is low
explore_lenses.summary: The practical burden is concentrated in communities with vaccination gaps and among people who cannot be fully protected by vaccination, rather than being spread evenly across the country.

claims.text: PAHO warned that renewed endemic measles can cause preventable deaths, particularly among vulnerable groups including children under age 5.

CDC says some people decline vaccination for religious or personal reasons, while others cannot receive it for medical reasons; both circumstances leave gaps that outbreak-control efforts must address.

CDC reported that U.S. kindergarten MMR coverage fell from 95.2% in the 2019-20 school year to 92.7% in 2023-24, and cited a study finding declining coverage in 78% of 2,066 counties studied across 33 states.

Provisional national surveillance data counted 4,641 indigenous measles cases through the week ending October 31, 2026, with especially large reported year-to-date totals in Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Utah, and Wisconsin.

explore_lenses.label: What would it take to regain status?
explore_lenses.title: A coordinated corrective plan is required
explore_lenses.summary: PAHO and U.S. public-health agencies describe re-elimination as achievable, but it requires interrupting sustained transmission and addressing the surveillance, access, and vaccination gaps that enabled it.

claims.text: PAHO says countries that lose elimination status must submit a corrective action plan describing how they will regain it, while intensifying efforts until transmission is interrupted and the outbreak is controlled.
CDC says its response will include encouraging MMR vaccination, expanding vaccine access, identifying communities at increased risk, and supporting rapid detection and outbreak response.

State and local public-health partners argue that high vaccination coverage, real-time surveillance, rapid outbreak investigations, community partnerships, and clear science-based information are necessary to re-eliminate measles.
CDC reports providing about $100 million in additional nationwide funding through most of 2027 for vaccine-preventable-disease prevention, outbreak response, epidemiology, and laboratory capacity.

story_report.summary: International health officials have withdrawn the United States’ measles-elimination designation after determining that a transmission chain that began on Jan. 20, 2025 continued for more than 12 months. The finding means endemic measles transmission has been re-established, ending 26 years of elimination status. The United States must now submit a corrective action plan and intensify efforts to interrupt transmission and control outbreaks; its elimination status for rubella and congenital rubella syndrome is unchanged.

sections.heading: Measles transmission and vaccination gaps
sections.body: The resurgence has been linked to unvaccinated populations, with reported transmission at its highest level in more than 30 years. CDC said kindergarten MMR coverage declined from 95.2% in the 2019-20 school year to 92.7% in 2023-24, and cited research finding falling coverage in 78% of 2,066 counties studied across 33 states. Some people decline vaccination for religious or personal reasons, while others cannot be vaccinated for medical reasons, CDC said.

sections.heading: Measles risks for vulnerable groups
sections.body: PAHO warned that renewed endemic measles can lead to preventable deaths, particularly among vulnerable groups including children younger than 5. Provisional national surveillance data recorded 4,641 indigenous measles cases through the week ending Oct. 31, 2026, with especially large year-to-date totals reported in Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Utah and Wisconsin. Weekly case counts remain subject to revision, and vaccination coverage and exposure risks can vary substantially within states and counties.

sections.heading: CDC response and restoration efforts
sections.body: CDC said it will encourage MMR vaccination, expand vaccine access, identify communities at increased risk, and support rapid detection and outbreak response. The agency also reported providing about $100 million in additional nationwide funding through most of 2027 for prevention of vaccine-preventable diseases, outbreak response, epidemiology and laboratory capacity. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the designation itself does not protect people; vaccination and stopping outbreaks are the operative public-health measures.

unresolved.text: The PAHO determination establishes sustained transmission during its review period, but does not by itself measure an individual’s current measles risk in a particular state or community.
PAHO and CDC did not provide a date for interrupting U.S. transmission or restoring elimination status.

related_stories.title: UK Imposes Sanctions on Israeli Firms Over West Bank Settlements
related_stories.summary: The UK government has announced sanctions against eight Israeli construction companies involved in building illegal settlements in the West Bank. This decision aims to hinder further settlement expansion, which the UK Foreign Office states undermines the prospects for a two-state solution. The sanctions also target a right-wing Israeli activist group linked to blocking aid efforts.

related_stories.title: Iran Denies Allegations of Planning 'Dirty Bomb' Attack on Washington
related_stories.summary: Iran has dismissed claims that it is plotting a 'dirty bomb' attack on Washington, labeling the reports as baseless. U.S. officials are reportedly debating the credibility of these allegations, while Trump stated that his administration is taking the threat seriously, despite the White House asserting there are currently no credible threats. Trump has issued a warning to Iran regarding these allegations.

related_stories.title: Iran Strikes U.S. Facility in Bahrain Amid Renewed Attacks on Arab Neighbors
related_stories.summary: On Tuesday, Iran launched a series of drone strikes targeting a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, marking its third attack on American military sites in the region within a few days. This escalation comes as Iran resumes strikes against its Arab neighbors after a two-month pause. In response, the U.S. targeted Iranian positions along a significant shipping route.
